summary: Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Martin Delhey earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and studied at Kyoto University. His career includes posts at Hamburg, Göttingen, Ryukoku University, Shandong University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Martin Gusinde studied at the University of Vienna from around 1924 to 1926. He later held an academic post at the Catholic University of America from circa 1949 to 1957.

Martin Haug was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. After earning his PhD at Tübingen and completing his habilitation at Bonn, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College and the University of Munich.

Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (1915–1923, 1936–1940) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Linguist and Indologist Martin Joachim Kümmel completed his MA, PhD, and habilitation at the University of Freiburg, also studying at Marburg under Eva Tichy and others. He served at Freiburg from 1999 to 2011 before becoming chairholder at Jena in 2013.

Martin Johannes Hammerich was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen, as well as under A. W. von Schlegel and H. H. Wilson. He served as docent in Sanskrit at Copenhagen and principal of Borgerdydskolen.

Martin King Whyte is a sociologist and sinologist who earned degrees at Cornell and Harvard. He taught at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University, and Harvard University, where he served as acting director of the Fairbank Center.
Martin Kraatz is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau and succeeded Käthe Neumann in 1968.

Martin Lehnert is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Freiburg and was attested in 2016 as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich.

Martin Lowenthal works in religious and Buddhist studies, having studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held positions at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Mills is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Edinburgh in 1997. He taught at the University of Sussex before joining the University of Aberdeen, where he became Chair in 2024.
Martin Novosad was a Buddhist studies practitioner who studied as a disciple under Nyanatiloka Mahathera in 1938. In 1940, he served as the leader of Verdant Hermitage.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Heidelberg and Munich. He served as professor at the University of Chicago and its Divinity School from 1990 to 2014, and at the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies in 2013.

Martin Schultze was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1855. He later served as director of the Höhere Töchterschule in Cüstrin (1869–1877) and rector at the Theodor-Mommsen-Schule (1877–1885).

Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Barend Jan Terwiel. He held an attested post at Hamburg in 2004 and is attested as a Council member of the Pali Text Society.

Martin Straube is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Michael Hahn. His appointments include research positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, the University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martin T. Adam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and studied at CIHTS. He has served as an instructor at McGill University.

Martin Williams completed an MA at Keele University (1972–1979). His career includes working as an IT Adviser for Powys County Council (1989–2007) and as Co-ordinator of the Naga Conciliation Group for the Religious Society of Friends (2011–2014).

Martin Willson was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna and completed an MA under Lambert Schmithausen. She served as Numata Professor at the University of Vienna (2021) and McGill University (2022).
